Please read the manuscript in /Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation. I had a new idea that I'd like to brainstorm, note that a parallel investigation is currently running within 01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy. 

The idea is motivated from the tensor network ansatz which is a common thread within investigations-6. I was thinking that maybe a natural place for the tensor network ansatz is to determine the spacing of the zeros. So consider making an (infinitely large) tree tensor network whose output is a zero spacing. It would be organized hierarchically in a spatial way, and I think it could be naturally thought of using a quantics tensor network, or TTN. Is this related to the idea in 01_qtt_newman_flow?

I’ll read the arithmetic-gap manuscript alongside the QTT–Newman work and check where the Jacobi investigation overlaps. Then I’ll look at what a tree would have to compute for its output to be a zero spacing.

The manuscript gives the tree a concrete output. Each spatial cell can carry a zero count and two moments, and merging two cells produces a term that measures the separation between zeros on opposite sides. I’ll work that out and identify what a tensor approximation would have to improve over a direct gap calculation.

Yes. **The existing QTT builds the field from the theta source. Your proposed tree could read a spacing from the field by combining neighboring regions of zero height.** The two networks would fit together naturally. In `01_qtt_newman_flow`, each tensor site represents one binary digit of the integration variable \(v\), and the contraction returns \(H_t(z)\) at a requested height. In your tree, each branch would represent a height interval. Quantics gives those intervals binary addresses, while the tree specifies how neighboring intervals combine. [QTT manuscript](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/01_qtt_newman_flow/manuscript/main.tex:253) · [Quantics construction](https://www.mis.mpg.de/publications/preprint-repository/article/2009/issue-55)

**There is an exact way for the spacing to emerge at a branch.** Imagine that the left child contains one zero and the right child contains one zero. Neither child has an internal spacing. Give each child its zero count and its first two power sums, obtained by contour integration of \(H'_t/H_t\). Those three quantities add when the cells merge. If the parent contains precisely the two zeros \(a,b\), its combined moments give
\[
2(a^2+b^2)-(a+b)^2=(b-a)^2.
\]
So the spacing appears at the first scale that brings the pair together, without supplying either zero ordinate as input. On a box symmetric about the real axis the same formula gives zero at a collision and a negative value for a nonreal conjugate pair. At time zero, half the positive Newman spacing is the usual zeta-ordinate spacing. [Arithmetic-gap manuscript, §2](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/manuscript/sections/02_pair_chain.tex:53)

I see two directions in your spatial intuition. **For determining a spacing at one time**, I’d start with one tree serving many adjacent gaps. For a single known pair, the internal contour edges cancel and the tree reproduces the direct outer-contour formula. Across many pairs, neighboring boxes can share arithmetic evaluations. That is where a low-rank tensor approximation could earn its cost. **For explaining how the surrounding zeros move one spacing**, the manuscript suggests a different tree. Keep the nearest neighbors individually and group progressively more distant zeros. Its root would supply the exterior interaction \(M\) in \(D'=2-4DM\), where \(D\) is the squared half-gap. That tree evolves an initial spacing. [Exterior interaction and gap chain](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/manuscript/sections/02_pair_chain.tex:167)

The parallel Jacobi investigation varies truncation degree \(N\) and moment orders \(p,q\). Your proposal varies **where and at what spatial scale the field is observed**. I’d test the fixed-time version first inside the existing QTT window \(40\le x\le80\): recover every adjacent gap from the source and compare total work with direct evaluation at the same certified accuracy. That tests the part an infinite tree would need most—the ability to reuse arithmetic information as more gaps come into view. I saved the explicit branch tensor, collision checks, and proposed comparison in the [spatial TTN brainstorm](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/notes/SPATIAL_TTN_ZERO_SPACING_BRAINSTORM_20261119.md).

Please include any notes within the brainstorm folder, and actually given that this spans multiple investigations, please place them in the brainstorm folder directly within investigations-6. Where do you propose that this investigation should go? Should it continue within 01_qtt_newman_flow, or should it be a new sub-investigation within 05_arithmetic_gap_continuation?
I’ll move the note to the shared Investigations 6 brainstorm folder, fix its links, and compare the existing branches’ research questions before recommending a home.

I recommend a **new sub-investigation under `05_arithmetic_gap_continuation`**, alongside `01_jacobi_integer_hierarchy`. I’d call it `02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings`.

The reason is the quantity you want the tree to determine. A QTT approximation can evaluate the Newman field accurately while leaving a close pair of zeros unresolved. The proposed investigation succeeds when it can count that pair and enclose its **spacing** to a stated accuracy. AGC already supplies the formula for that spacing and a direct calculation against which to measure any gain. QTT would contribute methods for sharing field evaluations across neighboring height intervals. The parallel Jacobi investigation asks how a gap estimate changes with truncation degree, so the two AGC branches could compare results on the same pair. [AGC pair formula](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/manuscript/sections/02_pair_chain.tex:53) · [QTT research plan](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/01_qtt_newman_flow/research-plan/01_QTT_RESEARCH_PLAN_20261113.md)

I’d make the first milestone **all consecutive spacings in one fixed height window at time zero**. Measure whether the tree can certify those gaps with less total work than direct evaluation at the same accuracy. That tests the distinctive promise of a spatial tree: work done for one pair can help resolve its neighbors.

I moved the note into the shared Investigations 6 brainstorm folder, added this recommendation, and verified the updated links. [Spatial tensor trees for zero spacings](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/brainstorm/notes/06_SPATIAL_TTN_ZERO_SPACING_20261119.md)

This sounds like a good plan, however I don't know if I agree on starting with analyzing a fixed height window. I think I'd prefer trying to determine the natural equations that determine how the tensor network is set up, and also how it evolves in time. This is more of an analytical investigation, and I think it could lead to more general results and an overall framework that could then be tested with explicit examples, but those examples would serve the purpose of testing the broader ideas and framework. 

Please make the new sub-investigation, following INVESTIGATION_SETUP_WORKFLOW. Please make the research program focus primarily on analytical frameworks that can lead to simplifications which could ideally lead to control over the gap chain dynamics and moments being studied in 05_arithmetic_gap_continuation.  \

I’ll set up the new AGC sub-investigation around the equations that define the spatial tree and govern its time evolution. I’ll use the parent manuscript’s gap chain and moment equations to identify what a tree would actually need to simplify.

The program now starts with a distinction the equations force. Two heat solutions can have exactly the same zeros inside a block and give the marked pair different velocities. The opening task therefore asks what information about the exterior must pass back down the tree. I’ve moved the fixed-window calculation to the later examples.

Created [Spatial tensor trees for zero spacings](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/README.md) under `05_arithmetic_gap_continuation`, alongside the Jacobi investigation.

The program starts with **what a block of zeros must exchange with its neighbors to evolve under Newman flow**. Two heat solutions can have exactly the same zeros inside a block and give those zeros different velocities. That gives the tree a concrete design question. One candidate passes the polynomial of the enclosed zeros *up* the tree and information about the exterior field *down* to each child. A second uses contour moments and their time evolution. The first analytical test is whether evolving two children and then merging gives the same result as merging first and evolving the parent. [Scientific overview](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/research-overview/01_AGC_ST_RESEARCH_OVERVIEW_20261119.md)

The plan then asks whether the tree exposes a cancellation or a controlled truncation that simplifies the complete gap drift \(D_t=2-4DM\) or the moment forcing \(12S_2+16DS_3\). Explicit examples come after an analytical claim gives them something to test. The original fixed-window idea remains in the [shared brainstorm](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/brainstorm/notes/06_SPATIAL_TTN_ZERO_SPACING_20261119.md) as one such possibility. [Research plan](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/research-plan/01_AGC_ST_RESEARCH_PLAN_20261119.md)

The setup is complete. **AGC-ST-B01 is ready for Astra/ultra** to select the block variables and formulate their evolution law. [Progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/research-progress/01_AGC_ST_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_20261119.md) · [Pasteable continuation prompt](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/notes/01_AGC_ST_CONTINUATION_AND_PROMPT_20261119.md)
Thinking about this some more, would it make more sense to output the actual zero instead of the spacing? Note the recent progress within the investigation before answering.
I’ll read the latest results in the spatial-tree investigation and its neighboring branches, then compare what the tree would need to recover an individual zero, a pair of zeros, and their spacing.

Yes. **I’d make an individual zero a primary output, evolve the polynomial of the marked block, and keep spacing as a quantity the tree can read from that polynomial.** The investigation’s recent progress gives a mathematical reason for all three choices.

The internally accepted split calculation shows that each block carries the monic polynomial of its enclosed zeros. Two child polynomials multiply to give the parent polynomial. A block containing one simple zero therefore carries \(P(z)=z-x(t)\): its coefficient gives the actual zero, and the exterior field determines its velocity. For a block containing two zeros, the natural state is \(P(z)=(z-c)^2-D\). It gives both locations \(c\pm\sqrt D\) and, for a real separated pair, the spacing \(2\sqrt D\). The coefficients \(c,D\) stay regular even when the two zeros meet and their individual labels become ambiguous. [Split generator](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/notes/02_AGC_ST_E01_SPLIT_GENERATOR_20261120.md:57) · [Local assessment](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/reviews/02_AGC_ST_LOCAL_GENERATOR_ASSESSMENT_20261120.md:23)

**What changes scientifically is that predicting a zero requires predicting the motion of the pair’s center.** For endpoints \(a,b\), write \(R\) for the logarithmic derivative of the field after removing the pair. The branch derived
\[
c'=R(a)+R(b),\qquad
D'=2-4DM,\qquad M=-\frac{R(b)-R(a)}{b-a}.
\]
The sum moves the pair together. The divided difference changes its separation. This explains why I’d keep the recent spacing work: it found that opposite displacements of left and right neighbors can cancel to first order in the gap forcing. Those same displacements can move the center. A tree designed to retain both effects could tell us more about the zero dynamics than either observable alone. [Pair equations](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/notes/03_AGC_ST_E02_PAIR_AND_FORCING_20261120.md:7) · [Paired forcing calculation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/notes/04_AGC_ST_E03_PAIRED_FORCING_20261120.md)

I’d therefore add one analytical question to the program: **starting from a pair localized at one time, can the tree bound its signed center displacement over time without being given the final zero positions?** Combined with the gap estimate, that would give enclosures for both actual zeros. I recorded the proposal and an exact example in which two even polynomial heat flows have the same marked zeros and the same instantaneous gap drift, yet their centers move in opposite directions. [Shared brainstorm addendum](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/brainstorm/notes/06_SPATIAL_TTN_ZERO_SPACING_20261119.md:13)

Can you write a new research overview, research plan and progress file with the modified program, again following the guidance in INVESTIGATION_SETUP_WORKFLOW, and with a similar overall goal and method, just with the modified idea?

I’ll write the new overview, plan, and progress register in the existing spatial-tree investigation. I’ll check the latest results and open work first, so the revised program can make individual zero locations a primary output while preserving what the branch has established about gaps.

The new documents distinguish what the tree already controls about a pair’s separation from the signed motion of its center. They also set a concrete test: start from independently localized zeros, withhold their final positions, and compare the predicted locations with a direct calculation using the same information.

I created the revised program in the existing spatial-tree investigation. **Its primary output is the location of an individual zero at another time.** The tree evolves the counted polynomial of a marked block. For a separated pair, its two zeros are \(c\pm\sqrt D\). The existing gap work controls relative motion through \(D\); the new analytical question is how the complete exterior controls the **signed displacement of the center** \(c\).

- [Research overview](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/research-overview/02_AGC_ST_ZERO_POSITIONS_RESEARCH_OVERVIEW_20261120.md) connects the new target to the accepted tree generator and forcing estimates, including what can be recovered through a collision.
- [Research plan](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/research-plan/02_AGC_ST_ZERO_POSITIONS_RESEARCH_PLAN_20261120.md) starts from an independently localized pair, withholds the final zero positions, and asks whether the tree can bound them as tightly as a direct calculation using the same information. Explicit examples come after a general claim is ready to test.
- [Progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/research-progress/02_AGC_ST_ZERO_POSITIONS_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_20261120.md) tracks the new position tasks and links to the separately tracked gap work already underway.

**AGC-ST-Z-B01 is ready to begin.** Its first decision is which information about the left and right exterior the tree must retain to predict center motion over time. [Pasteable continuation prompt](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/notes/AGC_ST_ZERO_POSITIONS_CONTINUATION_20261120.md)
